rationale: D2, data-informed. The laws of D1 on the third-generation droplet forward, revised after a train-only audit of D1. Law changes: no fast heat-up deficit (the measured rate in the first two seconds is 7-16 % above D1 in 12-13 of 16 sessions); the radiative clock shortens with initial diameter beyond what supercriticality gives (helium is left as in D1: the stage that follows the visible flame in helium has no law here); evaporation after the cool flame starts twice as fast and decays over 3.5 s. Encoder changes: the hot-flame run offset is trusted little (on train the law alone predicts the next seconds better than the law with the offset); the cool-flame run offset is read from the end of the prefix, where the cool flame is, and halved; the state at the cutoff is read from the end rate. Spread: 0.10 before a prefix and 0.06 after, twice the train residual, for unseen sessions; not chosen from validation. Every number typed by the author; no fit, no search.
